title: Initiate incident triage and automated severity routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current incident automation creates PagerDuty alerts and Slack pings but the initial signal payload lacks structured triage context (root traces, fingerprinting, probable subsystem, tentative severity). That causes manual triage overhead during high-severity events and inconsistent routing to escalation policies. Goal: Add an automated triage layer that enriches incoming alerts with condensed trace snippets, a fingerprint ID, a model-driven severity suggestion, and automatic routing rules that map to existing PagerDuty escalation policies and Slack response channels. The flow should be opt-in per alert rule, preserve full auditability, and allow manual override. The feature also includes creating a prefilled incident skeleton in the postmortem system (with basic telemetry links) when severity >= Sev-2.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a given test alert (see test harness link), the triage service attaches a 3-line trace summary, fingerprint, and severity suggestion to the PagerDuty payload and Slack message. 2) Routing rules send the alert to the correct PD escalation policy based on service fingerprint >=90% confidence. 3) Slack message contains 1-click ‘Create Incident Skeleton’ that creates a draft postmortem in /docs/incidents with prefilled headings and telemetry links. 4) End-to-end latency for enrichment must be <= 800ms added to alert processing path in 95th percentile. 5) All changes feature feature flag gating and audit logs for who/what routed the incident.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable for internal staging alerts only (2 teams). Collect metrics and manual triage feedback for 1 week. Phase 2 (beta): Enable for non-customer-facing alerts in prod (10% of rules) and expose opt-in toggle in Console alerting UI. Phase 3 (general availability): 100% opt-in default off; add auto-on for Dedicated customers per contract. Rollback plan: feature flag off, PD payload reverts to legacy fields; Slack messages remove enrichment attachment.
metrics: Primary: reduction in time-to-action (median triage time) by 25% for triaged alerts. Secondary: percentage of correct routing decisions (match to human-assigned escalation) >= 90% after model tuning. Performance: enrichment added latency 95p <= 800ms. Observability: histogram of enrichment times, success/failure counts, number of auto-created skeletons.
